aspects.says: How often an accessor is called during matching is the compiler's choice, so accessors should have no side effects.
basis: section:Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException
aspects.reason: the count is javac's behaviour and not promised, so a graded test must not pin it

aspects.says: A record pattern gets each component by calling its accessor, var components included, so it binds what an overridden accessor returns.
basis: section:Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException

aspects.says: An exception thrown by an accessor during a match arrives as MatchException with the original as its cause, so a catch for the original type misses it.
basis: section:Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException

aspects.says: A record pattern tests the record's type and binds each component by position; binding names are free, so two components of one type can be bound the wrong way round without a compile error.
basis: section:A Record Pattern Tests the Type, Then Binds Each Component by Position

aspects.says: For a generic record the compiler infers the type arguments from the matched value; component type patterns test the component's run-time class, and an explicit type argument that can't be checked is refused.
basis: section:A Narrower Type on a Component Is a Test, So a Payload Whose Type Changes Stops Matching
aspects.reason: inference and the refusal happen at compile time, where a test has no wrong solution that compiles; the run-time part is the narrower-type test the quiz checks

aspects.says: A narrower type on a component is a run-time test, not a cast: a value of another class makes the pattern fail without an exception, and the leftover branch receives it.
basis: section:A Narrower Type on a Component Is a Test, So a Payload Whose Type Changes Stops Matching

aspects.says: A record pattern never matches null at any depth, so a nested record pattern on a component that is null makes the whole pattern fail.
basis: section:A Record Pattern Never Matches null, at Any Depth; var and the Component's Declared Type Do

aspects.says: In Java 21 a record pattern goes only after instanceof or as a case label; the enhanced-for form was a Java 20 preview that was dropped, and the unnamed pattern _ is a preview until Java 22.
basis: section:A Record Pattern Tests the Type, Then Binds Each Component by Position

aspects.says: In Java 21 a pattern on a primitive component must be that primitive type or var.
basis: section:A Narrower Type on a Component Is a Test, So a Payload Whose Type Changes Stops Matching
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch

aspects.says: A component pattern that tests nothing (var, or the component's declared type) matches a null component and binds null, so a match does not promise non-null bindings.
basis: section:A Record Pattern Never Matches null, at Any Depth; var and the Component's Declared Type Do
